claim: The lab in card 'bit-reversal-swar' performs the same operation as the brev8 instruction (Zbkb).
rationale: REJECTED on 2026-09-11 review: the card verifies the full 64-bit bit reversal (checked against a naive bit-loop reference), while brev8 specifies reversal of bits within each byte. Different value mappings (bit 56 set reverses to bit 7 under the card's claim, to bit 63 under brev8). The "same operation" claim is withdrawn.

rationale: The card probes the medeleg CSR, not an instruction; no instruction exists to execute under QEMU for direct comparison.

instruction: csrs mstatus / csrrc mstatus (SIE bit manipulation)
claim: mstatus.SIE interrupt gating is a privilege CSR mechanism, not an instruction.
rationale: No corresponding RISC-V instruction to compare: the operation is a CSR control bit's effect on trap delivery, exercised via csrs/csrrc with no portable C equivalent. The verified property is the interrupt-delivery rule, not an opcode's arithmetic.

claim: sbrk heap management is a kernel interface, not an ISA instruction.
rationale: No RISC-V instruction implements sbrk: the property lives in xv6's sys_sbrk/growproc/deallocuvm path. The verified property is the kernel's heap bookkeeping, not a machine operation.

instruction: csrs sie / csrrc sie (SSIE bit manipulation)
claim: sie.SSIE per-interrupt gating is a privilege CSR mechanism, not an instruction.
rationale: No corresponding RISC-V instruction to compare: the operation is a CSR control bit's effect on interrupt delivery, exercised via csrs with no portable C equivalent. The verified property is the enable-gate rule (pending while clear, exactly one trap when set), not an opcode's arithmetic.

claim: sbrk(0) break query is a kernel interface, not an ISA instruction.
rationale: No RISC-V instruction implements sbrk: the property lives in xv6's sys_sbrk and growproc path. The verified property is the kernel's zero-increment query contract, not a machine operation.

claim: stval capture on ecall is a trap CSR behavior, not an ISA instruction.
rationale: No RISC-V instruction writes stval on an environment call: the property is what the hart records in the CSR when taking the trap. The verified behavior is the privileged architecture's trap-entry rule, not a computable instruction.

claim: satp MODE legality is a CSR field table, not an ISA instruction.
rationale: No RISC-V instruction validates satp.MODE: the property is whether a 4-bit field value names a defined translation scheme per Table 114. The module is a software table check against the spec, not a differential test against hardware execution.

claim: fflags NX accrual is a CSR flag behavior, not an ISA instruction.
rationale: No RISC-V instruction reports its own inexactness: the property is which accrued flag bit the hart sets in fcsr after an operation. The module tests the flag accrual, not a differential comparison against an instruction.

claim: frm write/readback is a CSR field behavior, not an ISA instruction.
rationale: No RISC-V instruction validates its own rounding-mode field: the property is whether the WARL frm field holds each written mode. The module tests CSR field write/readback, not a differential comparison against an instruction.

claim: Static rounding override is an instruction encoding behavior, not an ISA instruction.
rationale: No RISC-V instruction validates its own static-vs-dynamic rounding precedence: the property is which rounding the hart applies when the instruction's rm field names RNE while frm holds RDN or RUP. The module tests encoding override behavior, not a differential comparison against an instruction.

claim: Successive sbrk grows are a kernel interface, not an ISA instruction.
rationale: No RISC-V instruction implements sbrk: the property lives in xv6's sys_sbrk and growproc path. The verified property is the kernel's additive growth contract, not a machine operation.

claim: fflags UF accrual is a CSR flag behavior, not an ISA instruction.
rationale: No RISC-V instruction reports its own underflow: the property is which accrued flag bits the hart sets in fcsr after an underflowing operation. The module tests the flag accrual, not a differential comparison against an instruction.

claim: fflags OF accrual is a CSR flag behavior, not an ISA instruction.
rationale: No RISC-V instruction reports its own overflow: the property is which accrued flag bits the hart sets in fcsr after an overflowing operation. The module tests the flag accrual, not a differential comparison against an instruction.

claim: Directed-rounding quotient comparison is a rounding-mode behavior, not an ISA instruction.
rationale: No RISC-V instruction validates its own rounding: the property is which adjacent quotients the hart produces under frm=RDN versus frm=RUP. The module tests directed-rounding behavior, not a differential comparison against an instruction.

claim: The lab in card 'lab-119-onesc-add' performs the same operation as a one's-complement add instruction.
rationale: REJECTED 2026-09-12: RISC-V add computes (rs1 + rs2) mod 2^XLEN and discards the carry; no base or standard-extension instruction performs end-around-carry addition. The claim of an ISA mapping is withdrawn; the card ships as an honest algorithm card.

claim: The lab in card 'lab-127-sat-shl' performs the same operation as a saturating shift-left instruction.
rationale: REJECTED 2026-09-12: RISC-V sll/sllw truncate shifted-out bits silently; no base or standard-extension instruction saturates to all-ones on overflow. The claim of an ISA mapping is withdrawn; the card ships as an honest algorithm card.

claim: fflags DZ accrual is a CSR flag behavior, not an ISA instruction.
rationale: No RISC-V instruction reports its own divide-by-zero: the property is which accrued flag bit the hart sets in fcsr after the operation. The module tests the flag accrual, not a differential comparison against an instruction.

claim: Unsigned multiply-high is the mulhu instruction.
rationale: The module computes unsigned multiply-high in portable C, but without a specific chip citation for whereNeeded, the card ships with honest algorithm framing and no portability block.

claim: cbo.zero trap behavior is not a differential test against an instruction.
rationale: QEMU 8.2.2 does not execute cbo.zero; the probe records the illegal-instruction trap (mcause 0x2) and menvcfg writability. There is no executed instruction to compare against, so the card gets honest firmware/ISA framing without a portability block.

claim: pid uniqueness is not a differential test against an instruction.
